papers.title: De novo design of transmembrane accessory subunits for fold stabilization and expansion
papers.did: The lab developed an informatics-based de novo design strategy to create synthetic auxiliary subunits that interact with the TM helices of a model pentameric ion channel.
papers.found: Biochemical and structural characterization show the synthetic TM subunits bolster channel folding while maintaining function, and can be used to create larger multi-spanning designer proteins of custom topology.
papers.used: Informatics-based de novo design plus biochemical and structural characterization of a model pentameric ion channel.
papers.why: Motivates computationally designed accessory TM helices as potential pharmacological 'folding correctors' for diseases caused by membrane protein misfolding, and as tools for structural biology.
papers.anchor_quote: This proof-of-concept motivates the feasibility of computationally designed accessory TM helices as potential pharmacological chaperone “folding correctors” of membrane proteins in disease and as tools in structural biology.

papers.title: MemPPI platform for measuring and engineering membrane protein-protein interactions in mammalian cells via split nanoluciferase.
papers.did: The lab assessed and further developed the split luciferase (NanoBit) complementation system to establish expression constructs and conditions for quantifying transmembrane protein-protein interactions in human cells.
papers.found: Benchmarking with natural and synthetic memPPI pairs identified assay settings that robustly distinguish true positive interactions from co-expressed non-interacting pairs, with normalization of expression levels drastically improving dynamic range and consistency.
papers.used: Split NanoBit luciferase complementation assay, membrane expression constructs, and topology-controlled tagging strategies in mammalian cells.
papers.why: Provides a viable high-throughput platform for interaction analyses and protein engineering screens, such as TM binders targeting human membrane proteins, useful in protein science, design, and drug discovery.
papers.anchor_quote: We benchmarked the platform using a panel of natural and synthetic memPPI pairs with diverse architectures, insertion topologies, and trafficking patterns, finding assay settings that robustly distinguish true positive interactions from co-expressed non-interacting pairs.

papers.title: Programmed inhibition of an innate immune receptor via de novo designed transmembrane proteins
papers.did: The lab used a computational strategy to design polypeptides that target the transmembrane domain of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) directly within membranes.
papers.found: One synthetic protein binds TLR4's transmembrane domain and antagonizes NFκB signaling in human cells, demonstrating that precise transmembrane domain interactions drive cross-membrane conformational coupling.
papers.used: Computational design of lipid-embedded polypeptides targeting an apolar, sequence-motif-poor transmembrane domain, tested via NFκB signaling assays in human cells.
papers.why: Refines design principles for encoding stable protein interactions inside cellular membranes and expands the range of lipid-embedded targets accessible to designed molecules, relevant to therapeutic design.
papers.anchor_quote: One synthetic protein binds TLR4’s transmembrane domain and antagonizes NFκB signaling in human cells, proving that precise transmembrane domain interactions are essential for cross-membrane conformational coupling.

papers.title: Ab initio prediction of specific phospholipid complexes and membrane association of HIV-1 MPER antibodies by multi-scale simulations.
papers.did: The lab used multi-scale modeling (all-atom and coarse-grained simulations) to study how HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies dock onto HIV-like membranes.
papers.found: All-atom simulations of four antibodies consistently form phospholipid complexes at key CDR loop sites, and simulated bilayer affinity for PGZL1 maturation variants correlates with neutralization potency.
papers.used: All-atom and coarse-grained multi-scale molecular dynamics simulations of antibodies docked onto HIV-like lipid membranes.
papers.why: Reveals how lipid interactions anchor antibodies to membrane surfaces and highlights antibody features to prioritize in HIV vaccine design.
papers.anchor_quote: All-atom simulations of 4E10, PGZL1, 10E8, and LN01 docked onto HIV-like membranes consistently form phospholipid complexes at key complementarity-determining region loop sites, solidifying that stable and specific lipid interactions anchor bnAbs to membrane surfaces.

papers.title: Design principles of the common Gly-X6-Gly membrane protein building block.
papers.did: The lab used protein design and a fragment-based data-mining and sequence statistical inference method to engineer de novo transmembrane assemblies encoding Gly-X6-Gly and Ala-X6-Ala building blocks.
papers.found: A highly stable glycine-based design's X-ray structure shows Cα-H···O=C hydrogen bonding alongside extensive backbone-directed van der Waals packing, idealizing this motif as found in nature.
papers.used: Fragment-based data mining with cross-evolutionary structure-aligned covariance, de novo protein design, and X-ray crystallography.
papers.why: Data-driven design of core membrane protein structural motifs enables construction of increasingly complex lipid-embedded architectures.
papers.anchor_quote: A highly stable glycine-based design's X-ray structure hosts Cα-H∙∙∙O = C H-bonding alongside extensive backbone-directed van der Waals packing, idealizing features of this motif in Nature.

papers.title: De novo-designed transmembrane proteins bind and regulate a cytokine receptor.
papers.did: The lab designed de novo transmembrane proteins targeting the erythropoietin receptor (EpoR) TM domain in a custom binding topology that competes with receptor homodimerization.
papers.found: The designed TM proteins complex with EpoR in mammalian cells and inhibit erythropoietin-induced cell proliferation, with the synthetic complex outcompeting EpoR homodimerization in vitro at 1:1 stoichiometry.
papers.used: De novo transmembrane protein design, mammalian cell expression, and structural characterization of the TM complex.
papers.why: Shows that membrane protein TM regions can be targeted in custom-designed topologies, enabling new tools to regulate receptor signaling.
papers.anchor_quote: The TM proteins expressed in mammalian cells complex with EpoR and inhibit erythropoietin-induced cell proliferation.

papers.title: Transient water wires mediate selective proton transport in designed channel proteins.
papers.did: The lab performed molecular dynamics simulations to design transmembrane channels with stable water pockets interspersed by apolar segments capable of forming transient water wires.
papers.found: The minimalist designed channels conduct protons at rates similar to viral proton channels and are at least 10^6-fold more selective for H+ over Na+.
papers.used: Molecular dynamics simulations to design and analyze transmembrane proton channels.
papers.why: Informs the mechanisms of biological proton conduction and provides principles for engineering proton-conductive materials.
papers.anchor_quote: The minimalist designed channels conduct protons at rates similar to viral proton channels, and they are at least 10 6 -fold more selective for H + over Na + .

papers.title: Constructing ion channels from water-soluble α-helical barrels.
papers.did: The lab first used rational de novo design to generate water-soluble alpha-helical barrels with polar interiors, then modified the sequences to facilitate insertion into lipid bilayers.
papers.found: Single-channel electrical recordings and fluorescent imaging show monodisperse, cation-selective channels of unitary conductance, while an X-ray structure from the lipidic cubic phase reveals an alternative tightly packed, constricted state.
papers.used: De novo protein design, X-ray crystallography, single-channel electrical recordings, and fluorescent imaging.
papers.why: Demonstrates a multi-step strategy for converting water-soluble scaffolds into functional membrane ion channels, informing design of peptide-lipid interfaces.
papers.anchor_quote: Single-channel electrical recordings and fluorescent imaging of the peptides in membranes show monodisperse, cation-selective channels of unitary conductance.

papers.title: Protein design-scapes generated by microfluidic DNA assembly elucidate domain coupling in the bacterial histidine kinase CpxA.
papers.did: The lab built a hybrid valve- and droplet-based microfluidic system to deterministically assemble DNA parts encoding a combinatorial library of engineered histidine kinase CpxA variants with designed TM and S-helix domains.
papers.found: The S helix sets a basal catalytic activity that is further modulated by the TM domain, and a given TM motif can elicit opposing effects on catalytic activity depending on the S-helix variant.
papers.used: Microfluidic DNA assembly for combinatorial library generation and functional screening of engineered bacterial histidine kinase CpxA variants.
papers.why: Shows that the intervening HAMP domain passively transmits signals shaped by subtle changes in neighboring domains, informing how signaling responses can be engineered.
papers.anchor_quote: Surprisingly, we also find that a given TM motif can elicit opposing effects on the catalytic activity of different S-helix variants.
